José de San Martín. The Argentine military leader who liberated Chile and Peru from Spanish rule, earning the title Protector of Peru. A more conservative figure than Bolívar, he prioritized military success over political idealism and eventually withdrew from public life.

San Martín commanded the Army of the Andes, which crossed the Andes mountains to liberate Chile from Spanish control in 1817. He declared Peru's independence in 1821 and served as Protector until internal political conflicts forced his resignation. While in Peru, he met Bolívar, and the two disagreed on strategy. San Martín favored a constitutional monarchy, while Bolívar pushed for republicanism. After leaving office, San Martín spent his final years in voluntary exile in France, rejecting offers of power and refusing to meddle in South American politics. He is remembered for his professional military demeanor and his emphasis on institutional order over personality-driven leadership.
